page.layout: One page of text, one column, centred. A heading line at the top, then a verse poem of nine stanzas of two lines each, then a signature line. The faint mirrored print behind the text is show-through and is left out. The library stamp at the foot is not transcribed.

main_text.head: G. P. H. Christiano Lectori S.
main_text.p: N auis ut in medijs iactatur fluctibus, auster Dum furit, & rapidis æstuat æquor aquis:
Sic hominum variis agitatur vita procellis, Spem sola in Christi qui bonitate locant.
Impia Pontificum damnant qui dogmata, scriptis Quaeq; suis Monachi somnia vana docent.
At Deus insano vexatos turbine, tandem Respicit, & cunctis eripit ipse malis.
Pluribus exemplis sunt Biblia plena, prioris Historiæ & nostri temporis ista probant.
Exemplum hic etiam Friderico in principe rarum, Et Maria ipsius coniuge, Lector habes:
Quae subit optatos sanctissima fæmina portus, Dum tumidas medio gurgite versat aquas.
Atque graui posito rediuiua pondere carnis, Cum Christo summa viuit in arce poli:
Nostra ubi certa salus, æternaq; mansio pacis, Et requies nullo quæ peritura die.

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse (large mirrored title and imprint, faint) is left out. The library stamp is left out. The verse lines are run together within each stanza, as a stanza is one paragraph; the printed line breaks are not kept. The mark after "Quaeq" and "aeternaq" is a small superscript sign, read as q; with doubt. The first line of the poem and the word "Quae" have [?] marks omitted because they read clearly.
